# Introduction

This Rmd servers to fit models using PDAC data, mainly neutrophil features, to predict patient/FOV status.

# Library


```{r class.source='fold-show', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)
library(randomForest)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(scatterPlotMatrix)
library(reshape2)
set.seed(123)

```

# Load data

```{r class.source='fold-show', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

data <- read_csv("~/pdac/data/All_anno_clean_metadata_Tumor distance-inf_0328.csv")

```

## Summary

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

summary(data)

```

## Subset data

Previous EDA has determined that neutrophil seemed to have the largest difference between the relapse and non-relapse groups. Therefore, here we subset the data to only neutrophil.

```{r}

data_neutrophil <- data %>% 
  filter(cell_cluster == 'Neutrophil')

```

# Feature engineering

With the goal to predict relapse status at FOV/patient level and to utilize the variation of the single cell information to the fullest extend, we will engineer features using the following strategies and compare their performance:

1. Fit model on single cell level to predict each cell's relapse/non-relapse status then give the FOV level prediction by majority-vote principle.
2. Create FOV-level features that captures the distribution of each marker such as mean, variance, quantiles, etc. However, since we only have 31 data points, we will likely just use the mean to prevent $p > n$ issue.   
3. Using PCA to create a lower-dimensional representation of the features and use the mean PC of each FOV to build model. 

In addition, we will split neutrophil into two categories --- "near tumor" and "far from tumor". The above mentioned metrics should be calculated within each group.

Let's first define what's "near tumor" and "far from tumor":

- near tumor: $d\left(N,T\right) \leq 25 \mu m$.
- far from tumor: $d\left(N,T\right) \in \left(25, 100\right]\mu m$

Note that neutrophils that are either more than $100\mu m$ away from the tumor zone or within the tumor zone, i.e., $d\left(N,T\right) < 0$, will not be considered. 

```{r}

data_filtered <- data_neutrophil %>% 
  filter(distance_um <= 100 & distance_um > 0) %>% 
  mutate(neu_cat = ifelse(distance_um <= 25, 'near', 'far'))

```

## Strategy 2

```{r, message=FALSE}

functional_markers <- c("CD16", "MPO", "CD45.RA", "CD45RO", "HLA.DR", "Ki.67", "PD.1", "PD.L1")

fov_summary <- data_filtered %>%
  select(fov, all_of(functional_markers), Relapse, neu_cat) %>% 
  group_by(fov, Relapse, neu_cat) %>% 
  summarise(
    # Mean for each marker
    across(all_of(functional_markers), mean, .names = "{.col}_mean"),
    
    # # Median for each marker
    # across(all_of(functional_markers), median, .names = "{.col}_median"),
    # 
    # # Standard deviation for each marker
    # across(all_of(functional_markers), sd, .names = "{.col}_std"),
    # 
    # # 25th percentile
    # across(all_of(functional_markers), ~quantile(.,0.25), .names = "{.col}_q25"),
    # 
    # # 75th percentile
    # across(all_of(functional_markers), ~quantile(., 0.75), .names = "{.col}_q75"),
    
    # cell count per fov
    neutrophil_count = n(),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fov_summary <- fov_summary %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = neu_cat,
              values_from = colnames(fov_summary)[4:12])

```

Now let's check the correlation of these newly created variables. And no surprise, within each marker, a lot of these metrics are highly correlated since they are different summary statistics of the same distribution. To remedy potential multicollinearity, we will fit the model using some regularization method like LASSO or elastic net. 

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.pos='center', fig.width=8, fig.height=8, cache=TRUE}

categorical <- list(Relapse = c('Y', 'N'))

fov_summary %>% 
  scatterPlotMatrix(zAxisDim = 'Relapse', rotateTitle = TRUE, categoricalCS = "Set1", categorical = categorical)

```

# Model Fitting

We will try these models:

- Random forest
- Logistic regression with elastic net

## Random forest

### Strategy 1

Since this leverage on the original single cell information and we will use the majority-vote pricinple to assign a final label at the aggregated level, we will try both patient level prediction and fov level prediction.

#### FOV level

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

set.seed(123)

unique_fov <- unique(data_filtered$fov)

train_fov <- sample(unique_fov, round(0.7 * length(unique_fov)))

test_fov <- setdiff(unique_fov, train_fov)

train <- data_filtered %>% 
  filter(fov %in% train_fov) %>% 
  select(fov, Relapse, all_of(functional_markers), Age, Sex, BMI, Smoking_History, neu_cat) %>% 
  mutate(Relapse = factor(Relapse),
         Sex = factor(Sex),
         Smoking_History = factor(Smoking_History),
         neu_cat = factor(neu_cat))

test <- data_filtered %>% 
  anti_join(train) %>% 
  select(fov, Relapse, all_of(functional_markers), Age, Sex, BMI, Smoking_History, neu_cat) %>% 
  mutate(Relapse = factor(Relapse),
         Sex = factor(Sex),
         Smoking_History = factor(Smoking_History),
         neu_cat = factor(neu_cat))

```

```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,fig.pos='center', fig.height=15, fig.width=15}

# m1 <- randomForest(Relapse ~ Age + Sex + BMI + Smoking_History + CD16 + MPO + CD45.RA + CD45RO + HLA.DR + Ki.67 + PD.1 + PD.L1, data = train)

m1 <- randomForest(Relapse ~ CD16 + MPO + CD45.RA + CD45RO + HLA.DR + Ki.67 + PD.1 + PD.L1 + neu_cat, data = train)

test$pred <- predict(m1, test)

test_agg <- test %>% 
  group_by(fov, Relapse, pred) %>%
  count() %>% 
  slice_max(order_by = n, n = 1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-n)

cat("Accuracy:\n")
  
sum(test_agg$Relapse == test_agg$pred) / nrow(test_agg)

cat("Variable importance: \n")

varImpPlot(m1)

```

Difficulties:

- Couldn't really include any metadata because too many repeats, which artificially inflate the prediction accuracy and importance of those variables. That's a big deal breaker
- We subset to only neutrophils so we are basically classifying FOV with relapse/non-relapse predition on neutrophils. This is somewhat OK.

### Strategy 2

```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}

fov_summary <- fov_summary %>% 
  mutate(neu_near_prop = neutrophil_count_near/(neutrophil_count_far + neutrophil_count_near),
         neu_far_prop = neutrophil_count_far/(neutrophil_count_far + neutrophil_count_near))

set.seed(123)

unique_fov <- unique(fov_summary$fov)

train_fov <- sample(unique_fov, round(0.7 * length(unique_fov)))

test_fov <- setdiff(unique_fov, train_fov)

train <- fov_summary %>% 
  filter(fov %in% train_fov) %>% 
  mutate(Relapse = factor(Relapse))

test <- fov_summary %>% 
  anti_join(train) %>% 
  mutate(Relapse = factor(Relapse))

```


```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,fig.pos='center', fig.height=15, fig.width=15}

formula <- as.formula(paste('Relapse ~ ', paste(colnames(fov_summary[c(3:18, 21)]), collapse = " + ")))

m2 <- randomForest(formula, data = train)

test$pred <- predict(m2, test)

cat("Accuracy:\n")

sum(test$Relapse == test$pred) / nrow(test)

cat("Variable importance:\n")

varImpPlot(m2)

```

Difficulties:

- sample size too small while too many variables. Result very unreliable. Should abandon this approach. 

### Strategy 3

#### FOV approach, sample by patient. Repeated 3-fold cross validation

There are several caveats that need to be addressed:

1. Since each patient can have multiple FOVs, it's paramount to perform the training and testing split at patient level to prevent information leakage when fitting the model. 
2. Since our response variable --- relapse/non-relapse --- is a patient level feature, our effective sample size is small with 8 relapse patients and 4 non-relapse patients. With the limited sample size, we use a repeated 3-fold cross validation to get relatively more robust results.
3. Due to the limited sample size, all model fitting results should be taken cautiously. 

```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}

pca_near <- pca_plot_near %>% 
  mutate(bin = 'near')

pca_far <- pca_plot_far %>% 
  mutate(bin = 'far')

pca_df <- pca_near %>% 
  full_join(pca_far) %>% 
  mutate(bin = factor(bin))

```

```{r,fig.pos='center',echo=FALSE,fig.width=8, fig.height=8}

pca_summary <- pca_df %>% 
  group_by(patient, fov, relapse, bin) %>% 
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), mean, .names = "{.col}_mean")) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = bin,
              values_from = 5:12) %>% 
  ungroup()

categorical <- list(relapse = c('Y', 'N'))

pca_summary %>% 
  scatterPlotMatrix(zAxisDim = 'relapse', rotateTitle = TRUE, categoricalCS = "Set1", categorical = categorical)

```

```{r}

#####################################################
# 1. Setup Parameters
#####################################################

# Cross-validation parameters
k_folds <- 3         # Using fewer folds since you only have 12 patients
n_repeats <- 10      # Number of repetitions
n_trees <- 500       # Number of trees per forest

# Create data frame to store results
result_summary <- data.frame(
  fold = character(),
  repetition = numeric(),
  accuracy = numeric(),
  precision = numeric(),
  recall = numeric(),
  F1 = numeric(),
  var1 = character(),
  var2 = character(),
  var3 = character(),
  var4 = character(),
  var5 = character(),
  train_patients = character(),
  test_patients = character()
)

# Variable to store importance values across all folds
all_importance <- list()

all_models <- list()

#####################################################
# 2. Repeated K-fold Cross-Validation Function
#####################################################

run_cv <- function(pca_summary, formula, k_folds, n_repeats) {
  
  # Get unique patients by relapse status
  unique_relapse_patients <- unique(pca_summary$patient[pca_summary$relapse == 'Y'])
  unique_non_patients <- unique(pca_summary$patient[pca_summary$relapse == 'N'])
  
  # Create a data frame of patients with their relapse status
  patients_df <- data.frame(
    patient = c(unique_relapse_patients, unique_non_patients),
    relapse = c(rep('Y', length(unique_relapse_patients)), 
                rep('N', length(unique_non_patients)))
  )
  
  # Create a list to store all fold information
  all_folds <- list()
  fold_counter <- 1
  
  # Generate repeated k-fold splits at PATIENT level
  for (rep in 1:n_repeats) {
    # Set a different seed for each repetition
    set.seed(123 + rep)
    
    # Create stratified folds - keeping relapse and non-relapse patients balanced
    folds <- createFolds(patients_df$relapse, k = k_folds, list = TRUE, returnTrain = FALSE)
    
    for (fold in 1:k_folds) {
      # Get test patient IDs for this fold
      test_patient_indices <- folds[[fold]]
      test_patients <- patients_df$patient[test_patient_indices]
      
      # Get train patient IDs (all patients not in test)
      train_patients <- setdiff(patients_df$patient, test_patients)
      
      # Store in the list
      all_folds[[fold_counter]] <- list(
        rep = rep,
        fold = fold,
        train_patients = train_patients,
        test_patients = test_patients
      )
      
      fold_counter <- fold_counter + 1
    }
  }
  
  # Initialize result data frame
  results <- data.frame()
  
  # Run models for all folds
  for (i in 1:length(all_folds)) {
    # Get patients for this fold
    train_patients <- all_folds[[i]]$train_patients
    test_patients <- all_folds[[i]]$test_patients
    rep_num <- all_folds[[i]]$rep
    fold_num <- all_folds[[i]]$fold
    
    # Get FOVs corresponding to these patients
    train_fov <- pca_summary$fov[pca_summary$patient %in% train_patients]
    test_fov <- pca_summary$fov[pca_summary$patient %in% test_patients]
    
    # Create training and testing datasets
    train <- pca_summary %>% 
      filter(fov %in% train_fov) %>% 
      mutate(relapse = factor(relapse))
    
    test <- pca_summary %>% 
      filter(fov %in% test_fov) %>% 
      mutate(relapse = factor(relapse))
    
    # Check if we have both classes in the training set
    if (length(unique(train$relapse)) < 2) {
      warning(paste("Fold", i, "has only one class in training set. Skipping."))
      next
    }
    
    # Train random forest model
    m <- randomForest(formula, 
                      data = train, 
                      ntree = n_trees)
    
    if (rep_num == 1) {
      all_models[[fold_num]] <- m
    }
    
    # Make predictions
    test$pred <- predict(m, test)
    
    # Calculate metrics
    # Add small epsilon to prevent division by zero in edge cases
    epsilon <- 1e-10
    
    accuracy <- sum(test$relapse == test$pred) / nrow(test)
    
    recall <- sum(test$relapse == 'Y' & test$pred == 'Y') / 
      (sum(test$relapse == 'Y') + epsilon)
    
    precision <- sum(test$relapse == 'Y' & test$pred == 'Y') / 
      (sum(test$pred == 'Y') + epsilon)
    
    F1 <- 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall + epsilon)
    
    # Get variable importance
    var_imp <- varImp(m)
    var_imp$variable <- rownames(var_imp)
    
    # Store variable importance for later aggregation
    all_importance[[i]] <- var_imp
    
    # Get top 5 important variables
    top_vars <- var_imp %>% 
      slice_max(order_by = Overall, n = 5)
    
    imp_vars <- top_vars$variable
    
    # If fewer than 5 variables, pad with NA
    if (length(imp_vars) < 5) {
      imp_vars <- c(imp_vars, rep(NA, 5 - length(imp_vars)))
    }
    
    # Store results
    result_summary <- rbind(result_summary, data.frame(
      fold = fold_num,
      repetition = rep_num,
      accuracy = accuracy,
      precision = precision,
      recall = recall,
      F1 = F1,
      var1 = imp_vars[1],
      var2 = imp_vars[2],
      var3 = imp_vars[3],
      var4 = imp_vars[4],
      var5 = imp_vars[5],
      train_patients = paste(train_patients, collapse = ', '),
      test_patients = paste(test_patients, collapse = ', ')
    ))
  }
  
  return(list(result_summary = result_summary, all_importance = all_importance, all_models = all_models))
}

```

```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,echo=FALSE}

#####################################################
# 3. Run the CV and Analyze Results
#####################################################

# Define your formula based on your variable columns (columns 4-19)
formula <- as.formula(paste('relapse ~ ', paste(colnames(pca_summary[c(4:19)]), collapse = " + ")))

# Run the cross-validation
set.seed(123)  # Master seed for reproducibility
cv_results <- run_cv(pca_summary, formula, k_folds, n_repeats)

# Print overall summary statistics
cat("Average Performance Metrics Across All Folds:\n")
cat("Accuracy:", mean(cv_results$result_summary$accuracy, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Precision:", mean(cv_results$result_summary$precision, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Recall:", mean(cv_results$result_summary$recall, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("F1 Score:", mean(cv_results$result_summary$F1, na.rm = TRUE), "\n\n")

```

```{r, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,echo=FALSE}

#####################################################
# 4. Analyze Variable Importance
#####################################################

# Combine all importance data from different folds
all_imp_df <- bind_rows(cv_results$all_importance, .id = "fold")

# Calculate average importance for each variable
avg_importance <- all_imp_df %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_importance = mean(Overall, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_importance = sd(Overall, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_importance = min(Overall, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_importance = max(Overall, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower_ci = quantile(Overall, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper_ci = quantile(Overall, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    frequency = n()
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_importance))

# Print top 10 most important variables
print(head(avg_importance, 10))

# Count variable frequency in top 5
var_counts <- c(
  table(cv_results$result_summary$var1),
  table(cv_results$result_summary$var2),
  table(cv_results$result_summary$var3),
  table(cv_results$result_summary$var4),
  table(cv_results$result_summary$var5)
)

var_frequency <- data.frame(
  variable = names(var_counts),
  count = as.numeric(var_counts)
) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarize(total_count = sum(count)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_count))


print(head(var_frequency, 15))

```

```{r,fig.pos='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=15, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo = FALSE}

# Get top 5 variables
top_vars <- head(var_frequency$variable, 5)

# Function to create PDPs for a single model
create_pdps <- function(model, data, top_vars) {
  pdp_plots <- list()
  
  for (var in top_vars) {
    # Skip if variable doesn't exist in the data
    if (!var %in% colnames(data)) {
      warning(paste("Variable", var, "not found in data. Skipping."))
      next
    }
    
    # Create partial dependence data
    partial_data <- pdp::partial(model, pred.var = var, train = data)
    
    # Convert Y/N to 1/0 if needed for plotting
    if("yhat" %in% colnames(partial_data)) {
      # Already numeric
      plot_data <- partial_data
    } else {
      # Need to convert factor predictions to numeric
      # This assumes Y is the positive class
      plot_data <- partial_data %>%
        mutate(yhat = ifelse(grepl("Y", yhat.class), 1, 0))
    }
    
    # Create PDP plot
    p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = var, y = "yhat")) +
      geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
      geom_rug(sides = "b", alpha = 0.2) +
      ylab("Probability of Relapse") +
      xlab(var) +
      ggtitle(paste("Partial Dependence Plot for", var)) +
      theme_minimal() 
    
    pdp_plots[[var]] <- p
  }
  
  return(pdp_plots)
}

# Create PDPs for models from first repetition
if (length(cv_results$all_models) > 0) {
  # cat("\nCreating Partial Dependence Plots for top variables...\n")
  
  # Extract one model and corresponding data
  model1 <- cv_results$all_models[[1]]
  
  # Get data used for this model
  fold1_patients <- strsplit(cv_results$result_summary$train_patients[1], ", ")[[1]]
  fold1_fovs <- pca_summary$fov[pca_summary$patient %in% fold1_patients]
  model1_data <- pca_summary %>% 
    filter(fov %in% fold1_fovs) %>% 
    mutate(relapse = factor(relapse))
  
  # Create PDPs
  pdp_plots <- create_pdps(model1, model1_data, top_vars)
  
  # Arrange plots in a grid
  # do.call(gridExtra::grid.arrange, c(pdp_plots, ncol = 2))
  
  # Create ICE plots (Individual Conditional Expectation) for more detailed insights
  # ICE plots show how the prediction changes for each individual observation
  # cat("\nCreating ICE plots for top variables...\n")
  
  ice_plots <- list()
  
  ice_vars <- names(pdp_plots)[1:length(pdp_plots)] # Just do first 2 to save processing time
  
  for (var in ice_vars) {
    ice_data <- pdp::partial(model1, pred.var = var, train = model1_data, ice = TRUE)
    
    # If needed, convert factor predictions to numeric
    if(!"yhat" %in% colnames(ice_data)) {
      ice_data <- ice_data %>%
        mutate(yhat = ifelse(grepl("Y", yhat.class), 1, 0))
    }
    
    # Create ICE plot
    p_ice <- ggplot() +
      geom_line(data = ice_data, aes_string(x = var, y = "yhat", group = "yhat.id"), 
               alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
      geom_line(data = ice_data %>% group_by(!!sym(var)) %>% summarize(yhat = mean(yhat)),
               aes_string(x = var, y = "yhat"), color = "red", size = 1.5) +
      ylab("Probability of Relapse") +
      xlab(var) +
      ggtitle(paste("ICE Plot for", var, "(individual lines in gray, average in red)")) +
      theme_minimal() 
    
    ice_plots[[var]] <- p_ice
  }
  
  # do.call(gridExtra::grid.arrange, c(ice_plots, ncol = 2))
  
  
} else {
  cat("No models available for PDPs. Check if any folds completed successfully.\n")
}

```

```{r,fig.pos='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=15, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo = FALSE}

do.call(gridExtra::grid.arrange, c(pdp_plots, ncol = 2))

```


```{r,fig.pos='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=15, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo = FALSE}

do.call(gridExtra::grid.arrange, c(ice_plots, ncol = 2))

```

What is a **P**artial **D**ependency **P**lot (PDP)? In our case of a random forest model, replace the split criterion of a corresponding variable when it appears in a tree; run through all trees; calculate the corresponding prediction probability. 

I will use `PC4_mean_near` to demonstrate how to interpret partial dependency plots (PDP). We can observe that:

- When `PC4_mean_near` is negative, the probability of relapse stays relatively low.
- When `PC4_mean_near` crosses zero and becomes positive, there's a sharp increase in probability of relapse.
- Above 0, as `PC4_mean_near` continues to increase, the probablity of relapse also increases and gradually stabilizes. 

This indicates that higher values of `PC4_mean_near` are strongly correlated with increased probability of relapse.

What is a **I**ndividual **C**onditional **E**xpectation (ICE) plot? It's basically a PDP on observation level. It shows how the relapse probability for a individual observation (an FOV in our case) changes when we change the value of a variable. 

Now let's examine the composition of each of the top 5 important principle components to see if there is any biological insight.

```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,fig.pos='center',fig.height=15,fig.width=15}

pca_loading_df <- as.data.frame(pca_result_near$rotation[,c('PC2', 'PC6', 'PC8', 'PC4', 'PC5')]) %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = 'Marker')

pca_loading_melted <- melt(pca_loading_df, id.vars = "Marker",
                           variable.name = 'Component',
                           value.name = 'Loading')

pca_loading_melted %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Component, y = Marker, fill = Loading)) +
    geom_tile(color = "black", size = 1) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(high = "#c02c38", mid = 'white', low = "#144a74") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 20),
          axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20),
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 30)) +
    labs(title = "PCA Loading Matrix Heatmap",
         x = "Principal Component",
         y = "Marker",
         fill = "Loading Value") +
    # Add the values as text
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Loading)), 
              color = "black", size = 8) + 
  coord_fixed()

```
